claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child, Alex, who's 16 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask you a few more questions about Alex to determine your eligibility.

Since Alex is 16, their eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training. Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, college courses, or an approved training program)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in college or doing A-levels or anything like that. They finished school but haven't gone on to do any courses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a follow-up question about Alex's situation.

Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services? (If they have done so within the last 20 weeks, you may still be eligible for Child Benefit during that period.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't signed up with the careers service or anything like that. They just finished school and are figuring out what to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one more important question:

Is Alex currently working in paid employment for 24 hours or more per week, or are they claiming any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working that much - they don't have a job at all right now. And they're not claiming any benefits themselves either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. Let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on the information you've provided.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 16 years old
- Alex is not in approved education or training
- Alex has not registered with a careers service or armed services
- Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
- Alex is not claiming benefits in their own right

According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit for a child under 16. For children aged 16-19, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if they stay in approved education or training. There's also a 20-week extension available if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

Since Alex is 16, has left education, is not in approved training, and has not registered with a careers service or armed services, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex under the standard rules.

However, if Alex does decide to enroll in college, A-levels, or another approved education or training program in the future, you would be able to claim Child Benefit again at that point.
